elements.element: Commercial general liability coverage is at least USD 1,000,000 per occurrence.
elements.evidence: The retained clause requires "comprehensive general liability insurance with coverage of at least one million dollars ($1,000,000)" but states no per-occurrence basis; the limit basis is unspecified, so the per-occurrence anchor required by the element is absent.

elements.element: Commercial general liability coverage is at least USD 2,000,000 in the aggregate.
elements.evidence: No aggregate limit appears anywhere in clause 14 as rendered; only a single USD 1,000,000 CGL figure is stated.

elements.element: Professional errors and omissions coverage is at least USD 2,000,000.
elements.evidence: E&O remains at "at least one million dollars ($1,000,000)", below the USD 2,000,000 preferred limit.

elements.element: If Vendor processes Customer Data, cyber and privacy coverage is at least USD 5,000,000.
elements.evidence: The inserted cover is "cyber and privacy liability insurance with coverage of at least two million dollars ($2,000,000)", short of the USD 5,000,000 preferred limit; Contractor handles Company confidential records and systems, so the condition applies.

elements.element: Vendor maintains workers' compensation coverage as required by law.
elements.evidence: "Contractor shall maintain workers compensation insurance in the amount required by statute".

elements.element: Vendor provides certificates of insurance on request.
elements.evidence: "At Company's request, Contractor shall provide Company with certificates or other acceptable evidence of insurance ... evidencing the above coverage".

elements.element: Professional errors and omissions coverage is at least USD 1,000,000.
elements.evidence: Retained verbatim: "professional errors and omissions insurance for bodily injury, property damage or other losses with coverage of at least one million dollars ($1,000,000)".

elements.element: Cyber and privacy coverage is at least USD 2,000,000.
elements.evidence: Inserted: "and cyber and privacy liability insurance with coverage of at least two million dollars ($2,000,000)", operative for the term of the Agreement and covered by the existing certificates mechanic ("evidencing the above coverage").

reasons: The fallback checklist is complete: the existing E&O limit of USD 1,000,000 already satisfies the first element, and the single inserted phrase adds unconditional cyber and privacy liability cover of USD 2,000,000, satisfying the second.

The preferred level is not reached: no per-occurrence basis for CGL, no USD 2,000,000 CGL aggregate, E&O still at USD 1,000,000 rather than USD 2,000,000, and cyber at USD 2,000,000 rather than USD 5,000,000. To reach preferred the drafter would need to state "USD 1,000,000 per occurrence and USD 2,000,000 in the aggregate", raise E&O to USD 2,000,000 and cyber to USD 5,000,000.

Minimality holds: the edit is a single conjunctive insertion into the existing sentence; workers' compensation, CGL, E&O, the "in connection with the provision of Services" scope, the certificates mechanic and the material-change notice are all retained verbatim, and no survival tail, at-own-expense language or other model-language extras were imported.

Intent is preserved: the new cover sits inside the existing term-long obligation and is captured by "evidencing the above coverage", leaving no undefined term, dangling cross-reference or contradictory retained sentence.

Classification as a deviation is supportable because the clause as drafted failed the fallback outright (no cyber cover at all) for a contractor that accesses Company confidential records and computer systems.
